title: Watermark-driven batch formation with KV prefetch and GPU slab reserve for streaming chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a watermark-driven batch formation algorithm that prefetches per-session KV cache entries and reserves a small GPU memory slab to avoid OOMs during streaming chat completions. Goal: reduce 95th/99th latency tails for short-turn chat while preserving throughput for long-turn sessions and avoiding KV cache thrashing.
background: Current continuous batchers favor filling for throughput which increases tail latency for low-token chat turns and causes frequent KV cache evictions under mixed short/long session workloads. Prior experiments (ENG-7192, ENG-8321) show trade-offs between batching window size and KV memory churn; we need a solution that explicitly accounts for active KV pages and streaming small-response latency requirements.
proposed_solution: Introduce a watermark-based batch admission policy: each incoming streaming chat request arrives with a lightweight estimate of its remaining token budget (watermark). The batcher forms two soft-queues: fast-watermark (<= X tokens left) and background-watermark (> X). Fast-watermark requests are prioritized into low-latency micro-batches (size cap S_fast) that trigger KV prefetch for only the hot prefix pages. Background requests are aggregated into larger throughput batches. Additionally, reserve a small GPU slab (configurable, default 256MB) to hold transient KV prefetch buffers to prevent eviction storms during micro-batches. Implement predictive KV prefetching: use per-user prefix histograms to pre-warm 1-3 KV pages for fast-watermark requests. Add a memory accounting module so the scheduler rejects prefetched pages if they would exceed slab limits and falls back to best-effort streaming without prefetch.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: significantly lower P95/P99 latency for short-turn streaming responses; fewer KV eviction cascades; graceful degradation when memory is scarce.
- Cons: additional memory reserved reduces gross throughput during sustained high-concurrency loads; complexity in estimating remaining tokens and maintaining prefix histograms; potential stale prefetches for uncommon prompts.
- Mitigations: make slab size dynamic per-node; telemetry to measure prefetch hit rate and adjust heuristics automatically.
experiments: Planned A/B: route 10% of production traffic to watermark-batcher (micro-batch size 4, slab 256MB), 10% to baseline continuous batcher, remainder to control. Synthetic workloads: mix of short-turn (avg 6 tokens), medium (avg 64), long-turn (avg 1024) with 40/40/20 split. Measure latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, token/sec, KV prefetch hit rate, GPU memory high-water mark, and OOM events.
benchmark_results: Lab run (stage cluster, m60 nodes) -- short synthetic mix: watermark-batcher P95 140ms vs baseline 370ms; P99 340ms vs baseline 820ms. Throughput delta: -6% tokens/sec on peak sustained load with slab=256MB, but no increase in OOMs. Prefetch hit rate: 72% on stable prefixes, 26% for new prefixes. Observed fewer KV eviction spikes (peak evictions/min reduced by 63%).
tasks: Implement watermark header in API router
Extend batcher to maintain two soft-queues and batching caps
Add KV prefetcher bounded by GPU slab accounting
GPU slab reservation and dynamic sizing logic
Telemetry: prefetch hit/miss, slab utilization, tail latencies
decisions: Use token-remaining watermark from inference frontend rather than estimating in batcher (less churn)
Default slab size 256MB per-GPU with admin override
Micro-batch cap S_fast = 4, background cap S_bg = 64 to start; auto-adjust via telem
blockers: Need runtime API change to carry token-remaining header (ENG-10112 backlog)
GPU memory accounting primitives must be landed in node-agent (ENG-10009)
next_steps: Land routing header change in API gateway (owner: infra)
Merge PR for KV prefetcher prototype and run canary
Run 2-week A/B in staging with realistic production traces
notes: Implementation must be compatible with streaming function-calls and not force tokenization changes on clients. Keep prefetch probes read-only and idempotent to avoid stateful side effects. If slab is exhausted, batcher should gracefully fall back to best-effort streaming with an opt-out metric event.
review_feedback: PM: ensure we expose a runtime toggle per-customer for slab reservation
Design: prefetch UI in console to show hit rates per-model
Security: prefetch reads must respect tenant isolation and KMS policies
acceptance_criteria: P95 streaming chat latency for short-turn workload must decrease by >=45% vs baseline
No increase in OOM count across nodes for a sustained 2x load test
Prefetch hit rate > 50% on stable prefix traffic within 48h
